evidence.summary: Approved design (status line updated to approved in commit 2d3a66d). Intent: an installed agent builds a frameless, themed widget from one sentence without reading LifeDashboard sources. Decisions: the frame manifest field requires sdk 3 and parseManifest checks sdk before unknown keys; a frameless default applies only when an instance is created, so later package versions do not change existing instances; create installs dependencies, is non-interactive when a title is given or stdin is not a TTY, and derives a Latin slug by transliteration (no machine translation), with --slug as the override; the skill lives in create-widget and is copied as regular files into .claude/skills and .agents/skills, because the SDK is not installed yet when create runs; docs are rendered from platform constants with a drift check. Non-goals: the acceptance run (plan 4), npm publishing, title translation, other agents beyond the AGENTS.md baseline, MCP, and new gateway capabilities.

Ten tasks: Task 1 frame field, sdk 3 and sdk-first parsing; Task 2 frameless placement on the board; Task 3 dev shell starts in the manifest frame; Task 4 slug and lifedashboard- folder; Task 5 CLI title prompt, flags and dependency install; Task 6 skill and full AGENTS.md; Task 7 generated package docs; Task 8 starter prompt in the packages dialog; Task 9 README; Task 10 whole-repo typecheck, test run and pack check. Global constraints: no new dependency except vite 8.3.2 as a devDependency of create-widget (approved by the user on 2026-10-20). All plan checkboxes are unchecked, which records nothing either way. The plan's review commits (0435396, 4f46b75, b7a4ca9) are reviews of the plan document.

risks.text: Installed skill copies lag behind later SDK upgrades, because the skill ships with create-widget and is copied at create time (spec, Skill).
Widgets built with sdk 3 need a dashboard that supports level 3; accepted in the spec because nothing was published yet.
Test runs for the new create, contracts and widget-sdk behavior are not recorded, so the unit-level behavior is not verified by any record in the repository.

decisions.text: The frame field lives in the manifest and needs sdk 3; parseManifest checks sdk before unknown keys so that a newer manifest gets 'needs a newer LifeDashboard' instead of 'unknown field'. Rationale: an installed parser cannot be changed by a new SDK.

The manifest frame default applies only when an instance is created; later package versions do not change existing instances, and board export and import are unchanged. Rationale: appearance already persists in the board, and the user can change the frame afterward.

create derives the technical name by transliteration and never translates titles to English, because automatic translation adds complexity. Titles with no Latin form need --slug. Rationale: the user gives the title in any language; the technical name is derived automatically.

create is non-interactive whenever the title is given or stdin is not a TTY, so an agent never hangs; it installs dependencies with the package manager that ran it. Rationale: one command must be enough for the user.

The skill ships in create-widget and is copied as regular files into .claude/skills and .agents/skills, not symlinked. Rationale: the SDK is not installed when create writes files, and symlinks can break when a project is copied or zipped.
Package docs are rendered from platform constants and committed; a drift test compares them with a fresh render. Rationale: docs must state the enforced limits and names, not hand-copied values.

The only new dependency is vite 8.3.2 as a devDependency of create-widget, used to bundle contracts into the CLI; the user approved it on 2026-10-20. Rationale: the real title check ships with the CLI without a hand-copied rule.
